---
title: "Feedforward Neural Network"
description: "A neural network in which information flows from inputs toward outputs without cyclic connections."
term: "Feedforward Neural Network"
letter: "F"
category: "Deep Learning"
difficulty: "Beginner"
---

## Simple explanation

A feedforward neural network passes information from its input layers
through hidden layers to an output. It does not send activations back
around a cycle as part of its forward computation.

## Technical explanation

A feedforward network composes functions such as affine transformations
and nonlinear activations:
$h^{(l)}=f^{(l)}(W^{(l)}h^{(l-1)}+b^{(l)})$. A multilayer perceptron is
a common fully connected feedforward architecture. Training can still
use backpropagation, which propagates gradients backward through the
computation graph.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Feedforward networks are a foundational architecture and a useful
baseline for structured prediction. The distinction between forward
computation and backward gradient calculation helps explain how neural
networks are trained.

## How it works

Each layer receives the previous layer's output, applies learned
parameters and possibly a nonlinearity, and passes its result onward.
The final layer produces predictions for a task.

## Practical example

A dense feedforward network can classify tabular records by transforming
feature values through hidden layers and producing one score per class.

## Common misconceptions

- “Feedforward” describes the direction of inference, not how training
  gradients are computed.
- A network can be feedforward without every layer being fully connected.
- Feedforward networks are not limited to classification; they can also
  perform regression and other tasks.
